body.rationale: The governing IPS (config/ips.yaml) is still a draft, so I weighed IPS breaches as provisional but still informative. I am max_sharpe and cannot rank myself. First choice is resampled_efficient_frontier. It is the only portfolio that passes every hard IPS check with diffuse weights (effective N 13.3), and it hedges the estimation error in the return forecasts that my own method suffers from. Its weaknesses are thin drawdown headroom (-24.3% vs -25%) and a gamma description that is internally inconsistent. Neither is fatal. Second is pc_researcher. It has the best ex-ante Sharpe among the diversified candidates (0.51), a backtest Sharpe of 0.70, a shallow drawdown (-10.9%), and a lowest-of-the-compliant CRO risk of 0.33. Its volatility and tracking-error breaches are modest and it is the most implementable low-risk anchor. Reviewers flagged that its Sharpe of 0.51 does not follow from the stated floor, so that needs checking. Third is black_litterman. It is intra-category and passes the IPS, with consistent execution (effective N 6.1 recomputed and confirmed). Its main weakness is boundary-tuned volatility. Fourth is cvar_minimization. It passes the IPS, has the best backtest Sharpe among the passing portfolios (0.74), and brings a tail-aware, non-covariance view that adds diversity in a late-cycle regime. Its risks are a tail sample dominated by a few crises and a volatility target tuned to the band edge. Fifth is tail_risk_parity. It has a coherent downside-risk method and a sensible 6.0 effective N, and it spans the non_traditional family without the single-vertex problem of the adversarial diversifier. Why first beats fifth: resampled_efficient_frontier meets all hard IPS limits and sits inside the 8-12% band with real diversification. tail_risk_parity breaches return, volatility and tracking error, and it is largely a cash and short-Treasury portfolio. That makes it a weaker base for the CIO to build from, even though it is cleanly executed. The bottom flag is hierarchical_risk_parity. It is about 92% cash with effective N of 1.4. It breaches return, volatility and tracking error, and it treats cash as a clustering node. Its reviewers also found a technical error in the description of the risk budgets. It offers the CIO the least to build on. I did not flag adversarial_diversifier because its orthogonality has ensemble value, but I left it out of my top five because of the three IPS breaches and its single-asset vertex.
